title: Découverte des lignes
oneGoal: Students recognize that lines are everywhere in their environment
connectionToPrevious: Starting our artistic adventure - we're going to be visual detectives!
realWorldConnection: Lines in classroom objects, clothing patterns, and body movements
materials: Large visual cards showing different lines

mindsOn.description: Take students on a 'detective walk' around classroom. Use magnifying glasses to 'discover' lines on desks, chairs, windows. Teacher models excitement: 'Je vois une ligne!' while tracing lines with finger in air.
mindsOn.tpr: Trace lines in the air with whole arm movements while saying words

action.description: Students move between stations: 1) Creating straight lines with tape on floor, 2) Making curved lines with their bodies, 3) Drawing lines in sand tray. Teacher demonstrates each station first.
visualSupports: Tape lines on floor as examples
action.tpr: Straight arms for 'droit', curved body sway for 'courbe', finger tracing for 'ligne'

consolidation.description: Gather in circle. Each student shares one line they found using 'J'ai trouvé une ligne...' Students can point, gesture, or draw in air instead of speaking if needed.
consolidation.tpr: Students show their line discovery with body movements

decisionPoints.situation: If students seem restless during detective walk
decisionPoints.action: Add more physical movement - have them march, tiptoe, or dance between line discoveries

decisionPoints.situation: If students struggle with vocabulary
decisionPoints.action: Focus on gestures only - finger straight up for 'droit', wavy arm for 'courbe', pointing for 'ligne'

decisionPoints.situation: If students finish stations early
decisionPoints.action: Have them become 'line teachers' helping friends or creating new line combinations

emergencyBackup.plan: Use student bodies as lines - lie down straight for 'droit', curl up for 'courbe'. Dance with line movements to music.

title: Lignes avec le corps
oneGoal: Students create different types of lines using their bodies and gestures
connectionToPrevious: Yesterday we found lines everywhere - today we BECOME the lines!
realWorldConnection: Body movements create invisible lines in dance and sports
materials: Large paper strips showing line types

mindsOn.description: Quick review of yesterday's lines using body movements. Teacher calls out 'ligne droite!' and students make straight body line. Add yesterday's vocabulary with actions.
mindsOn.tpr: Full body becomes the line shape - straight, curved, angular

action.description: Teach new line types through movement: zigzag (elbows sharp, changing directions), ondulé (flowing wave movements), spirale (spinning inward/outward). Students create a group line dance combining all types.
action.tpr: Sharp elbow movements for zigzag, flowing arms for ondulé, spinning whole body for spirale

consolidation.description: Small groups (3-4 students) perform their favorite line type for others to guess. Audience can join in if they recognize the line movement.
consolidation.tpr: Whole body expression for line types, audience copying movements

decisionPoints.situation: If students are too energetic
decisionPoints.action: Add slow-motion challenge - perform line movements in slow motion for control

decisionPoints.situation: If students are shy about movement
decisionPoints.action: Start with seated arm movements only, gradually add standing and whole body

decisionPoints.situation: If space is limited
decisionPoints.action: Focus on upper body and arm movements, use finger dancing on desk surface

emergencyBackup.plan: Teacher provides rhythm with clapping or simple songs. Students can create their own rhythm sounds for line movements.

title: Lignes émotionnelles
oneGoal: Students understand that different line qualities express different feelings
connectionToPrevious: Our bodies made amazing lines yesterday - now let's give our lines feelings!
realWorldConnection: How we draw when happy versus sad shows in our line quality

mindsOn.description: Show emotion face cards. Students make their bodies into lines that match feelings: happy lines bounce and curve up, sad lines droop down, angry lines are sharp and jagged.
mindsOn.tpr: Bouncy curved movements for happy, drooping arms for sad, sharp jabbing motions for angry

action.description: Students paint lines that show feelings. Happy lines in bright colors with curves, sad lines that droop in blue/purple, angry lines in red with jagged strokes. Teacher demonstrates first with exaggerated emotions.
action.tpr: Painting movements match emotions - light bouncy strokes for happy, heavy slow strokes for sad, quick sharp strokes for angry

consolidation.description: Display paintings around room. Students walk around and guess which emotion each painting shows. Artist can confirm with gesture/movement, no words needed.
consolidation.tpr: Students show the emotion with their body when their painting is discussed

decisionPoints.situation: If students resist painting
decisionPoints.action: Start with finger tracing emotions in air, then move to dry brushes on paper, then add paint

decisionPoints.situation: If students mix up emotions
decisionPoints.action: Pair each emotion with a simple song or chant with matching movements

decisionPoints.situation: If paint creates chaos
decisionPoints.action: Switch to oil pastels or thick markers with same emotion-line concepts

emergencyBackup.plan: Use colored pencils or crayons. Focus more on body movement emotions and tracing emotions in sand trays or on rough paper.

title: Chasse aux formes
oneGoal: Students identify basic shapes (circle, square, triangle) in their environment
connectionToPrevious: Lines helped us show feelings - now let's see what happens when lines connect to make shapes!
realWorldConnection: Shapes appear in signs, windows, wheels, and everyday objects

mindsOn.description: Students make shapes with their bodies. Demonstrate: arms in circle above head for 'cercle', arms and legs making square corners for 'carré', three students forming triangle together.
mindsOn.tpr: Round arms for circle, angular arm/leg positions for square, three students connecting for triangle

action.description: Using shape binoculars, students hunt for shapes around classroom and school. When they spot a shape, they place matching sticker on checklist and celebrate with shape dance move. Work in pairs for support.
visualSupports: Shape binoculars with cutout viewing holes
action.tpr: Specific dance move for each shape found - spinning for circles, marching in square pattern, jumping with arms up for triangles

consolidation.description: Students share favorite shape discoveries by showing location and making shape with their body. Others try to guess which shape before the reveal.
consolidation.tpr: Full body shape-making, pointing gestures, group copying of shape movements

decisionPoints.situation: If students get overwhelmed by too many shape choices
decisionPoints.action: Focus on just one shape at a time - complete circle hunt, then move to squares, then triangles

decisionPoints.situation: If students can't find shapes
decisionPoints.action: Teacher points out obvious examples first, gradually let students discover more subtle ones

decisionPoints.situation: If students finish hunt quickly
decisionPoints.action: Challenge them to find unusual or hidden shapes, or create shapes using classroom objects

emergencyBackup.plan: Hide large paper shapes around classroom beforehand. Students hunt for hidden shapes instead of naturally occurring ones.

title: Création de lignes libres
oneGoal: Students practice making various line types with drawing tools
connectionToPrevious: We found amazing shapes everywhere - now let's create special lines using different tools!
realWorldConnection: Different drawing tools create different line qualities for different purposes

mindsOn.description: Students explore how different tools make different lines. Demonstrate thick marker making 'épais' lines, thin pencil making 'mince' lines, cotton swab making 'pointillé' dots. Let students feel the tools and make test marks.
mindsOn.tpr: Wide arm gestures for thick lines, delicate finger movements for thin lines, dabbing motion for dotted lines

action.description: Students rotate through three stations: 1) Thick line weather patterns (sun rays, rain), 2) Thin line delicate drawings (grass, hair), 3) Dotted line pictures (flowers, paths). Each station has visual examples and encourages experimentation.
action.tpr: Hand movements match line quality while drawing - bold strokes, gentle touches, rhythmic dotting

consolidation.description: Students choose their favorite line creation to share. They demonstrate the hand movement needed to make that type of line while others guess 'épais', 'mince', or 'pointillé'.
consolidation.tpr: Students demonstrate the physical motion needed for their line type, others copy the movement

decisionPoints.situation: If students struggle with tool control
decisionPoints.action: Start with larger paper and bigger arm movements, gradually work toward smaller, more controlled lines

decisionPoints.situation: If students rush through stations
decisionPoints.action: Add challenge cards at each station with specific line patterns to create or copy

decisionPoints.situation: If students are frustrated with thin lines
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them that thin lines take practice, show how even 'mistakes' can become art

emergencyBackup.plan: Use fingers with different pressures - light touch for thin lines, firm press for thick lines, fingertip dots for pointillé. Draw in sand tray or on textured surfaces.

title: Formes avec les mains
oneGoal: Students create shapes using finger painting and hand printing techniques
connectionToPrevious: We made amazing lines with tools - now let's use our hands to create new shapes!
realWorldConnection: Hands can create shapes in sand, clay, and other materials

mindsOn.description: Students practice making new shapes with their hands in the air before painting. Rectangle (hands making corners), ovale (hands forming oval), losange (diamond with fingertips touching). Add the shapes from previous lesson for review.
visualSupports: Mirror for students to see their hand shapes
mindsOn.tpr: Specific hand positions for each shape, full arm movements to show shape boundaries

action.description: Students create shapes using hand prints and finger painting. Make rectangles by printing hand four times in corners, ovals by curving finger paints, diamonds by using fingertips. Encourage experimentation and multiple attempts.
visualSupports: Shape examples made with hand prints
action.tpr: Hand movements for painting match the shape being created, students can trace shapes in air while paint dries

consolidation.description: Students walk around to see everyone's hand-print shapes. They can point to shapes they recognize and make the hand gesture for that shape. Artist nods or shakes head to confirm guesses.
visualSupports: Artwork displayed on desks or walls
consolidation.tpr: Hand shape gestures for each shape type, pointing, celebratory movements for correct guesses

decisionPoints.situation: If students are messy or worried about getting dirty
decisionPoints.action: Start with one finger painting only, use wet wipes frequently, emphasize that mess is part of art

decisionPoints.situation: If students can't make recognizable shapes
decisionPoints.action: Focus on the attempt rather than perfection, help them see shapes in their 'accidents'

decisionPoints.situation: If paint is too runny or thick
decisionPoints.action: Adjust consistency or switch to using hands to trace shapes in sand/salt trays

emergencyBackup.situation: Finger paints unavailable or classroom restrictions
emergencyBackup.plan: Use clay or playdough to create 3D shapes with hands. Students can press hands into clay to make shape impressions.

title: Lignes racontent des histoires
oneGoal: Students use different lines to illustrate simple stories or experiences
connectionToPrevious: Our hands made beautiful shapes - now let's use lines to tell stories about our adventures!
realWorldConnection: Maps use lines to show paths and journeys we take

mindsOn.description: Teacher tells simple story using body movements and lines: 'Je marche en ligne droite à l'école' (walk straight), 'Je tourne en ligne courbe au parc' (curved walking), 'Mon chat fait un chemin zigzag' (zigzag movements). Students act out with teacher.
mindsOn.tpr: Walking in different line patterns, full body story acting, directional movements

action.description: Students create a 'map' of their journey from home to school using different lines. Straight lines for sidewalks, curved lines for turns, zigzag lines for stairs or hills. They can add simple drawings of landmarks along their path.
action.tpr: Tracing path lines with finger while drawing, walking movements to show journey parts

consolidation.description: Students share their journey maps by tracing the path with their finger and making the appropriate line movements (straight walking, curved turning, zigzag climbing). Others can guess what each line represents.
visualSupports: Maps displayed in center of circle
consolidation.tpr: Finger tracing combined with body movements that match each line type

decisionPoints.situation: If students don't remember their route to school
decisionPoints.action: Help them create an imaginary journey or a journey through the classroom/school instead

decisionPoints.situation: If students make very complex maps
decisionPoints.action: Praise their detail but encourage them to pick the three most important parts of their journey

decisionPoints.situation: If students finish early
decisionPoints.action: Have them create a journey map for a favorite story character or pet

emergencyBackup.situation: Students struggle with personal journey concept
emergencyBackup.plan: Use a familiar story like 'Three Little Pigs' and create the pigs' journey using different lines for different parts of their adventure.

title: Motifs avec des formes
oneGoal: Students create simple repeating patterns using basic shapes
connectionToPrevious: Our lines told wonderful stories - now let's put shapes together to make patterns!
realWorldConnection: Patterns appear in clothing, wallpaper, and nature around us

mindsOn.description: Create simple body patterns as a group. Teacher leads: 'circle arms, square arms, circle arms, square arms' - students follow and predict what comes next. Add triangle arms. Students take turns leading a simple pattern.
mindsOn.tpr: Circular arm movements, square corner arms, triangle arms up, rhythmic pattern repetition

action.description: Students use shape stamps to create repeating patterns on long paper strips. Start with simple AB patterns (circle-square-circle-square), then try ABC patterns. Display example patterns but encourage original creations.
action.tpr: Rhythmic stamping motions, counting patterns with finger pointing, clapping pattern rhythms

consolidation.description: Students wear their pattern strips as belts, headbands, or hold them up as banners. Walk around room showing off patterns while others clap to the rhythm of their pattern. Audience tries to continue the pattern.
consolidation.tpr: Clapping to match pattern rhythm, walking in pattern tempo, pointing to pattern elements

decisionPoints.situation: If students make random shapes instead of patterns
decisionPoints.action: Start with just two shapes and physically help them alternate: 'your turn circle, now square, now circle...'

decisionPoints.situation: If students create very complex patterns
decisionPoints.action: Celebrate their creativity and help them teach their pattern to a friend

decisionPoints.situation: If stamps don't work well
decisionPoints.action: Switch to drawing patterns with crayons or use pattern blocks to build patterns instead

emergencyBackup.plan: Use cut paper shapes to glue patterns, or create patterns with pattern blocks and copy them by drawing.

title: Lignes et nature
oneGoal: Students observe and recreate natural line patterns from plants and animals
connectionToPrevious: We made patterns with shapes - now let's discover the amazing patterns nature makes with lines!
realWorldConnection: Tree branches, leaf veins, and animal stripes are natural line patterns

mindsOn.description: Students examine real leaves and branches with magnifying glasses. Teacher guides observation: 'Regardez les lignes!' Point out veins in leaves, branch patterns, tree bark lines. Students trace these lines with their fingers.
mindsOn.tpr: Finger tracing on real objects, branching arm gestures to show branch patterns, leaf-like hand movements

action.description: Students create artwork inspired by natural line patterns. They can: 1) Draw leaf vein patterns, 2) Create branch patterns like trees, 3) Make animal stripe patterns. Use nature objects as reference and encourage close observation.
action.tpr: Drawing movements that match natural patterns - flowing for branches, delicate for leaf veins, rhythmic for stripes

consolidation.description: Display student artwork. Others try to guess what natural element inspired each drawing (leaf, branch, animal stripes). Artists can give clues using gestures or show the natural object that inspired them.
visualSupports: Natural reference objects available for comparison
consolidation.tpr: Gesture clues about natural elements, pointing comparisons between art and nature objects

decisionPoints.situation: If natural objects aren't available
decisionPoints.action: Use high-quality nature photos or take students on a brief outdoor observation walk if possible

decisionPoints.situation: If students struggle to see patterns
decisionPoints.action: Use your finger to trace patterns on the natural objects while students watch, then have them try

decisionPoints.situation: If students want to draw realistically
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them but focus on the line patterns rather than perfect representation

emergencyBackup.plan: Use online nature videos or photos on screen. Students can trace line patterns they see in the air, then draw them on paper.

title: Formes géométriques composées
oneGoal: Students combine basic shapes to create more complex forms and objects
connectionToPrevious: Nature showed us amazing line patterns - now let's build with shapes like nature builds with elements!
realWorldConnection: Houses, cars, and toys are made by combining basic shapes
materials: Large cut paper shapes in multiple sizes

mindsOn.description: Using pattern blocks, students work in pairs to build simple objects (house, car, robot) using only basic shapes. Teacher shows example: triangle on top of square makes a house. Students explore combinations.
mindsOn.tpr: Building motions with hands, stacking gestures, pointing to shape combinations

action.description: Students create pictures by combining paper shapes. They can make: houses (triangles + squares + rectangles), animals (circles + ovals), vehicles (rectangles + circles). Encourage experimentation and personal creativity.
visualSupports: Variety of pre-cut shapes in different sizes
action.tpr: Placing and arranging motions, building up gestures, creation celebration movements

consolidation.description: Students present their shape creations. They point to each shape used and count how many shapes total. Audience can guess what object was created before the reveal.
consolidation.tpr: Pointing to individual shapes, counting with fingers, guessing gestures from audience

decisionPoints.situation: If students glue shapes too quickly
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them to try different arrangements before gluing, have a 'no-glue exploration time' first

decisionPoints.situation: If students are frustrated with shape placement
decisionPoints.action: Remind them that there's no wrong way to combine shapes, help them see beauty in unexpected combinations

decisionPoints.situation: If students run out of shapes
decisionPoints.action: Have them trade shapes with classmates or use drawing to add details to their shape constructions

emergencyBackup.plan: Use pattern blocks to build creations and have students draw their constructions. Or use sidewalk chalk outside to draw large shape combinations.

title: Cultures et motifs
oneGoal: Students explore line and shape patterns from different cultures
connectionToPrevious: We built amazing things with shapes - now let's see how people around the world decorate with patterns!
realWorldConnection: Every culture decorates objects with special line and shape patterns

mindsOn.description: Show examples of patterns from different cultures (African kente cloth, Indigenous beadwork, Mexican pottery, etc.). Students observe and identify familiar shapes and lines. Teacher explains these are special decorations from different families around the world.
visualSupports: Real cultural objects or high-quality photos
mindsOn.tpr: Tracing pattern elements with finger, respectful observation postures, appreciation gestures

action.description: Students choose one cultural pattern style to explore and create their own version. Provide simple templates or guides but encourage personal interpretation. Focus on the shapes and lines used rather than exact replication.
action.tpr: Pattern-drawing movements that match cultural styles, rhythmic pattern creation, respectful handling of cultural examples

consolidation.description: Students share their pattern creations and identify which culture inspired them. Discuss how all cultures make beautiful decorations and how patterns help people express their identity and traditions.
consolidation.tpr: Presenting postures, respectful listening, appreciation clapping, pattern-tracing for sharing

decisionPoints.situation: If students don't understand cultural context
decisionPoints.action: Focus on appreciation of beautiful patterns made by families far away, emphasize respect and admiration

decisionPoints.situation: If students try to copy exactly
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them to be inspired by the patterns but make their own version using the same shapes and lines

decisionPoints.situation: If cultural materials are limited
decisionPoints.action: Use online resources or library books with cultural pattern examples, focus on 2-3 clear examples

emergencyBackup.plan: Focus on patterns from students' own family backgrounds. Ask students if their families have special decorations or patterns at home.

title: Expression personnelle
oneGoal: Students create original artworks expressing their feelings using lines and shapes
connectionToPrevious: We learned how different cultures express themselves - now it's time to express ourselves with lines and shapes!
realWorldConnection: Art helps us share our feelings with others through visual language
materials: Various art supplies (paper, crayons, markers, paint)

mindsOn.description: Students look in mirrors and identify how they feel today. Practice making lines and shapes in the air that match their feelings. Review emotional lines from Lesson 3 and add new feeling words as needed.
mindsOn.tpr: Facial expressions in mirror, air-drawing of emotional lines, full body expression of feelings

action.description: Students create a personal artwork using lines and shapes to express something important to them - their family, their favorite place, their dreams, or their feelings. Provide gentle music and encourage experimentation with all learned techniques.
action.tpr: Personal choice of drawing movements, self-directed art-making gestures, individual expression through movement

consolidation.description: Students sit quietly with their artwork and reflect on what they created. They can share with a partner or just appreciate their own work. Focus on the process and personal meaning rather than appearance.
consolidation.tpr: Quiet appreciation gestures, gentle pointing to artwork elements, reflective postures

decisionPoints.situation: If students feel overwhelmed by open-ended choice
decisionPoints.action: Provide simple prompts like 'draw your family using shapes' or 'show your favorite season with lines'

decisionPoints.situation: If students compare their work negatively
decisionPoints.action: Emphasize that each artwork is special because it comes from their unique heart and mind

decisionPoints.situation: If students finish very quickly
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them to add more details or create a second piece about a different feeling or memory

emergencyBackup.plan: Make it less personal - have them create artwork about their favorite animal or color instead, focusing on technique rather than emotion.

title: Critique et appréciation
oneGoal: Students observe and discuss how lines and shapes work in artworks and daily life
connectionToPrevious: We expressed ourselves through art - now let's become art detectives and look carefully at art around us!
realWorldConnection: Looking carefully at art and design helps us see beauty everywhere

mindsOn.description: Students become official 'art detectives.' Practice looking closely at one simple artwork, finding all the lines and shapes they can see. Teacher demonstrates careful observation with magnifying glass and excited discovery voice.
mindsOn.tpr: Detective postures, careful observation movements, pointing discoveries, excited recognition gestures

action.description: Set up classroom as mini gallery with art prints. Students move through in pairs, using detective skills to find and mark lines and shapes they recognize. Each artwork has simple questions: 'What shapes do you see?' 'Which lines look happy/sad?'
visualSupports: Art prints at student eye level
action.tpr: Gallery walking postures, pointing at art elements, partner discussion gestures, careful observation movements

consolidation.description: Students share their most interesting art discovery. They point to what they found and demonstrate the line or shape with their body. Others can add their observations about the same artwork.
consolidation.tpr: Presenting postures, pointing to art elements, body shape demonstrations, attentive listening positions

decisionPoints.situation: If students get distracted by art content rather than elements
decisionPoints.action: Use abstract artworks or focus their attention with specific 'missions' like 'find all the circles'

decisionPoints.situation: If students rush through observations
decisionPoints.action: Add timer challenge - spend full 2 minutes looking at each artwork before moving on

decisionPoints.situation: If vocabulary is too challenging
decisionPoints.action: Focus on pointing and gesturing, let students show what they see rather than describe verbally

emergencyBackup.plan: Use student artwork from previous lessons as gallery pieces, or investigate line and shape elements in classroom decorations and displays.

title: Portfolio et réflexion
oneGoal: Students compile their work and reflect on their learning about lines and shapes
connectionToPrevious: We've been art detectives looking at art - now let's look at all the amazing art we've created!
realWorldConnection: Keeping artwork helps us see how our skills grow and change

mindsOn.description: Display all student artwork from previous lessons around the room. Students walk around and try to remember which lesson each piece came from. Teacher helps by giving clues about activities: 'This is from when we painted with our hands!'
visualSupports: Lesson reference cards for teacher prompts
mindsOn.tpr: Memory recall gestures, pointing recognition, walking tour movements, excited remembering expressions

action.description: Students organize their artwork into portfolios, choosing their favorites for the front. For each piece, they reflect on simple questions: 'What do you like about this?' 'What was fun to make?' Use pictures and gestures more than writing.
visualSupports: Simple reflection sheets with picture prompts
action.tpr: Organizing and arranging movements, reflection thinking postures, sharing gestures with teacher

consolidation.description: Students hold their portfolios and share one thing they learned about lines and shapes. This can be done through gesture, pointing to artwork, or simple words. Celebrate growth and artistic journey.
consolidation.tpr: Proud holding postures, sharing gestures, celebration movements, appreciation clapping

decisionPoints.situation: If students can't remember lesson activities
decisionPoints.action: Re-demonstrate key movements or techniques from each lesson to trigger memory

decisionPoints.situation: If students are critical of their early work
decisionPoints.action: Focus on growth and learning, show how each piece taught them something new

decisionPoints.situation: If portfolio organization is overwhelming
decisionPoints.action: Help students choose just 3-5 favorite pieces and focus on those for reflection

emergencyBackup.situation: Student artwork is incomplete or missing
emergencyBackup.plan: Focus on memories and learning instead of physical pieces. Students can recreate favorite techniques or demonstrate what they learned through movement and gesture.

title: Lignes dans l'espace
oneGoal: Students practice creating three-dimensional line sculptures with wire and pipe cleaners
connectionToPrevious: Our portfolios showed our amazing flat artwork - now let's make lines that stand up in space!
realWorldConnection: Sculptors use lines in space to create artwork we can walk around

mindsOn.description: Students work in pairs to create 3D line sculptures with their bodies. One student poses making a line shape (straight, curved, zigzag) while partner walks around them to see the line from different angles. Switch roles.
mindsOn.tpr: Line posing with whole body, walking around to observe, changing viewpoints, pointing to line elements from different angles

action.description: Students create 3D line sculptures using pipe cleaners and craft wire. Start with simple lines that stand up, then encourage curves, spirals, and combinations. Attach to small base so sculptures can stand independently.
action.tpr: Twisting and bending motions with hands, building up gestures, viewing sculptures from different angles

consolidation.description: Display all sculptures on tables. Students walk around the gallery, viewing each sculpture from different angles. They can point out favorite line elements and demonstrate the hand movements needed to create similar lines.
consolidation.tpr: Gallery walking, viewing from different angles, hand movement demonstrations, appreciation gestures

decisionPoints.situation: If students struggle with 3D concept
decisionPoints.action: Start with simple standing lines, gradually add curves and bends, emphasize that sculptures can be seen from all sides

decisionPoints.situation: If wire materials are difficult to manipulate
decisionPoints.action: Use thicker pipe cleaners only, or help students work in pairs to support each other's construction

decisionPoints.situation: If sculptures don't stand up well
decisionPoints.action: Provide larger bases or help students create wider, more stable base designs

emergencyBackup.plan: Use playdough or clay to create 3D line sculptures by rolling and shaping. Students can make standing line forms that can be viewed from all angles.

title: Formes en collage
oneGoal: Students practice shape recognition and composition through paper collage techniques
connectionToPrevious: We built amazing 3D line sculptures - now let's layer shapes to create beautiful collages!
realWorldConnection: Magazine pictures are made of shapes that can be cut and rearranged

mindsOn.description: Using pre-cut paper shapes, students experiment with layering shapes on top of each other. Demonstrate how shapes can overlap, hide behind each other, or peek out from behind. Students practice the concept of 'superposer' (layering/overlapping).
mindsOn.tpr: Layering hand movements, stacking gestures, peeking movements to show shapes hiding and revealing

action.description: Students create collages by cutting shapes from colored paper and magazines, then arranging and layering them on background paper. Encourage experimentation with overlapping and composition. They can create abstract designs or simple representational images.
action.tpr: Cutting motions, arranging and rearranging movements, layering gestures, composition planning movements

consolidation.description: Students present their collages and point out where shapes are layered or overlapped. Others can identify shapes they recognize and discuss how the layering creates visual interest.
consolidation.tpr: Presenting gestures, pointing to overlapped areas, shape identification movements, layering demonstrations

decisionPoints.situation: If students struggle with scissors
decisionPoints.action: Provide more pre-cut shapes or use tear-paper technique instead of cutting

decisionPoints.situation: If students glue too quickly without planning
decisionPoints.action: Encourage arrangement planning before gluing, have a 'no-glue exploration time'

decisionPoints.situation: If students make very busy collages
decisionPoints.action: Suggest they choose their favorite elements and remove some for cleaner composition

emergencyBackup.plan: Use pre-torn paper shapes or digital shape arranging if technology is available. Focus on layering and composition concepts rather than cutting skills.

title: Lignes de mouvement
oneGoal: Students practice drawing action lines that show movement and energy
connectionToPrevious: Our collages showed shapes in interesting arrangements - now let's show movement and action with special lines!
realWorldConnection: Comic books use special lines to show speed and movement

mindsOn.description: Students use ribbon scarves to create movement lines in the air. Fast movements make quick lines, slow movements make flowing lines. Teacher demonstrates how different movements create different line qualities in the air.
visualSupports: Ribbon scarves for visible movement trails
mindsOn.tpr: Fast and slow movement with scarves, whole body movement creating line trails, rhythm variations for different line types

action.description: Students create drawings that show movement using special action lines. They can draw: running figures with speed lines, bouncing balls with arc lines, spinning objects with spiral lines. Encourage experimentation with line direction and spacing.
visualSupports: Comic book examples of movement lines
action.tpr: Drawing movements that match the action being drawn - fast strokes for speed, curved motions for bouncing, spiraling for spinning

consolidation.description: Students show their action drawings and demonstrate the movement their lines represent. Others guess what action is being shown based on the line types and directions.
consolidation.tpr: Action demonstrations to match drawn movement lines, guessing gestures, copying movement patterns

decisionPoints.situation: If students don't understand movement concept
decisionPoints.action: Start with simple movements like bouncing balls, use real objects to show movement paths

decisionPoints.situation: If students focus too much on realistic drawing
decisionPoints.action: Emphasize that movement lines are special effects, like magic lines that show action

decisionPoints.situation: If students make chaotic scribbles
decisionPoints.action: Guide them to specific movements - choose one action and practice just those movement lines

emergencyBackup.plan: Use finger movement in air to practice action lines, or draw large movement lines with sidewalk chalk outside.

title: Motifs personnalisés
oneGoal: Students practice creating their own unique patterns using learned shapes and lines
connectionToPrevious: We showed movement with special lines - now let's invent our own special patterns using everything we've learned!
realWorldConnection: Designers create new patterns for fabric, wallpaper, and products

mindsOn.description: Students become 'pattern inventors.' Review all the shapes and lines they've learned, then brainstorm combinations that no one has tried before. Use body movements to test pattern ideas before drawing them.
visualSupports: Review charts of all learned shapes and lines
mindsOn.tpr: Inventive thinking gestures, combination movements mixing different line types, creative brainstorming postures

action.description: Students create their own unique patterns using combinations of shapes, lines, and techniques from all previous lessons. Encourage them to name their patterns and think about where their pattern might be used in real life.
action.tpr: Creative pattern-making movements, personal artistic expression, invention celebration gestures

consolidation.description: Students present their unique patterns as professional designers. They show their pattern, demonstrate how to make part of it, and suggest where it could be used (clothing, wallpaper, etc.).
consolidation.tpr: Professional presentation postures, demonstration of pattern-making techniques, pointing to pattern applications

decisionPoints.situation: If students copy existing patterns exactly
decisionPoints.action: Encourage them to change one element to make it uniquely theirs - different colors, sizes, or combinations

decisionPoints.situation: If students feel overwhelmed by choices
decisionPoints.action: Limit options to 2-3 techniques or provide simple starting prompts for pattern creation

decisionPoints.situation: If students create very complex patterns
decisionPoints.action: Help them identify the core repeating unit and practice making it clearly

emergencyBackup.plan: Focus on pattern planning and design using paper and pencil, or create patterns using natural materials found outside.

title: Collaborations créatives
oneGoal: Students practice teamwork by creating large group artworks using lines and shapes
connectionToPrevious: We invented amazing personal patterns - now let's work together to create something bigger than any of us could make alone!
realWorldConnection: Many public artworks are created by teams of artists working together

mindsOn.description: Students sit in small groups (3-4) and plan a collaborative artwork. Each person will contribute their specialty from previous lessons. Practice taking turns and listening to each other's ideas.
mindsOn.tpr: Planning discussion gestures, turn-taking movements, listening postures, agreement gestures

action.description: Groups work together to create large collaborative artworks. Each student contributes their strengths - one might add shapes, another patterns, another movement lines. Encourage communication and shared decision-making.
action.tpr: Cooperative working movements, sharing gestures, collaborative problem-solving postures, group celebration movements

consolidation.description: Groups present their collaborative artworks to the class. Each team member points out their contribution and explains one thing they learned from working together.
consolidation.tpr: Group presentation postures, pointing to individual contributions, teamwork appreciation gestures

decisionPoints.situation: If groups have conflicts over artistic choices
decisionPoints.action: Guide them to combine ideas rather than choose one, teach compromise through art techniques

decisionPoints.situation: If some students dominate the collaborative process
decisionPoints.action: Assign specific roles or areas of the artwork to each student, use timer for turn-taking

decisionPoints.situation: If groups finish at very different rates
decisionPoints.action: Early finishers can add refinements or help other groups with encouragement and ideas

emergencyBackup.plan: Switch to individual work on one large class mural where everyone contributes their own section connected to others.

title: Galerie d'exposition
oneGoal: Students practice presentation skills by displaying and explaining their line and shape artworks
connectionToPrevious: We created beautiful collaborative art together - now let's celebrate all our artistic learning by sharing it with others!
realWorldConnection: Art galleries and museums help artists share their work with the community

mindsOn.description: Students help transform classroom into professional gallery space. They practice being museum guides, learning to walk quietly, speak clearly, and point respectfully at artwork. Practice gallery etiquette.
mindsOn.tpr: Quiet walking movements, respectful pointing gestures, clear speaking postures, professional gallery behaviors

action.description: Students take turns being artists and audience members. Artists stand by their work and share one thing about their artistic learning journey. Audience members practice respectful appreciation and asking kind questions.
action.tpr: Professional artist presentation postures, respectful audience listening, appreciation gestures, celebration movements

consolidation.description: Gather in circle for final celebration of artistic growth. Each student shares one favorite memory from their line and shape learning journey. Celebrate everyone's artistic development and creativity.
consolidation.tpr: Celebratory postures, memory sharing gestures, appreciation movements, community celebration

decisionPoints.situation: If students are nervous about presenting
decisionPoints.action: Allow pointing and gesturing instead of speaking, pair shy students with confident partners

decisionPoints.situation: If exhibition becomes chaotic
decisionPoints.action: Use small group rotations instead of whole class movement, add structure with specific viewing times

decisionPoints.situation: If students focus on comparing artwork
decisionPoints.action: Redirect to appreciating each person's unique artistic journey and growth

emergencyBackup.plan: Create individual portfolio sharing in pairs or small groups, focus on personal artistic growth rather than public exhibition.
